summary: For ages 5–7, help children learn WHERE tropical rainforests are: a belt around the warm middle of the Earth near the Equator, with the three great blocks being the Amazon (South America), the Congo (Central Africa), and Southeast Asia — and that they occur on every continent except Antarctica (too cold) and Europe (an age-appropriate simplification for tropical rainforests). Tie location to cause (hot and wet near the Equator). A labelled world map or globe makes the spatial pattern concrete; place-the-rainforest games and recall checks support it. Keep location tied to the climate reason, not just a list of names.
misconceptions: Rainforests are scattered randomly — they form a belt near the warm Equator
There is only one rainforest (the Amazon) — there are great rainforests in Africa and Asia too
Rainforests grow everywhere, even cold places — not in Antarctica (too cold) or Europe
All rainforests are in South America — the Congo and Southeast Asia have huge ones as well
Rainforests are near where I live — for most children they are far away near the Equator

activities.title: Tap the Equator belt on a world map
steps: Look at a world map with a warm Equator line drawn across the middle.
Tap the Equator line and watch green rainforest patches bloom in a band near it (with gaps for oceans, mountains and drier places).

Tap each of the three regions in turn: South America (the Amazon spreads with a giant river), Central Africa (the Congo appears), and Southeast Asia (a scatter of steamy green islands) — each with a one-line label.
Use a globe-spin control to see the green rainforest patches lying in a band around the warm middle of the Earth.
Lift a flap answering 'Which continents have NO tropical rainforest?' revealing Antarctica (too cold) and Europe.
activities.insight: Rainforests are not scattered randomly: they lie in patches in a band around the warm, wet middle of the planet near the Equator, with three great blocks in South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia, and no tropical rainforest in Antarctica (too cold) or Europe.

activities.title: Place-the-rainforest map game / find the green belt
steps: Drag to spin a globe and find the green belt around the warm middle.
Play a place-the-rainforest game: drag or place rainforest markers onto South America, Central Africa, and Southeast Asia on a world map.
Say aloud where each region is and why rainforests grow there (hot and wet near the Equator).
activities.insight: Actively placing the regions builds the location idea and the equatorial-belt pattern through the child's own actions.

activities.title: Check and explain: where and why
steps: Point to where the Equator is on the globe and say whether rainforests are near it or far from it.
Name at least two continents that have large rainforests.
Answer: Why couldn't a tropical rainforest grow at the freezing cold South Pole?
Answer the diagnostic: Could there be a big tropical rainforest at the North Pole, or right here in Britain? Where on Earth do tropical rainforests grow, and why there and not just anywhere?
activities.insight: A secure answer places tropical rainforests in a belt near the Equator across several continents (Amazon/Congo/SE Asia) AND explains they grow there because it is hot and wet all year — not at the cold poles and not in Britain, where it is too cool.

checkQuestion: Could there be a big rainforest at the North Pole, or right here in Britain? Where on Earth do rainforests grow, and why there and not just anywhere?
checkAnswer: Rainforests grow in a belt around the middle of the Earth, near the Equator — like the Amazon in South America, the Congo in Central Africa, and Southeast Asia — because it's hot and wet there all year. It's too cold at the North Pole and not hot and wet enough in most of Britain, so tropical rainforests don't grow in those places.
